title: The integral compact-support direct image of a constructible complex is constructible
statement: Let $K_0$ be a field, let $X,Y$ be finite-type $K_0$-schemes and $f:X\to Y$ a separated finite-type $K_0$-morphism [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties]. Fix a prime $\ell$ invertible in $K_0$, a finite extension $E/\Ql$ with valuation ring $\mathcal O_E$ and uniformizer $\varpi_E$, and put $A_{E,n}=\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^n$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Choose a compactification $c=(j,\bar f)$ of $f$ [def-weil-compactifications-refinements] and let $Rf_{!,n}=R\bar f_{*,n}j_!:D(X_{\mathrm{proet}},A_{E,n})\to D(Y_{\mathrm{proet}},A_{E,n})$ be the compact-support candidate attached to $c$ [def-weil-compact-support-candidate]. Let $K\in D^b_c(X,\mathcal O_E)$ be an object of the derived-complete integral category [def-weil-derived-complete-integral-detailed], and put $K_n=K\otimes^L_{\mathcal O_E}A_{E,n}$, the derived reduction [def-weil-integral-derived-reduction]. The objects $M_n=\operatorname{Res}_nRf_{!,n}K_n$ of $D(Y_{\mathrm{proet}},\mathcal O_E)$, with $\operatorname{Res}_n$ the restriction of scalars of the completed coefficient sheaf [def-weil-completed-integral-coefficients] applied termwise [lem-weil-restriction-of-scalars-exact], form an inverse system whose transition map $M_{n+1}\to M_n$ is $\operatorname{Res}_{n+1}$ applied to the composite of $Rf_{!,n+1}$ of the reduction map $K_{n+1}\to\operatorname{Res}^{A_{E,n+1}}_{A_{E,n}}K_n$ with the isomorphism $Rf_{!,n+1}\operatorname{Res}^{A_{E,n+1}}_{A_{E,n}}\cong\operatorname{Res}^{A_{E,n+1}}_{A_{E,n}}Rf_{!,n}$ of [lem-sf-compact-support-restriction-of-scalars]. Then every derived limit $M=R\varprojlim_nM_n$ of this system in $D(Y_{\mathrm{proet}},\mathcal O_E)$ [def-weil-derived-limit] lies in $D^b_c(Y,\mathcal O_E)$: it is derived complete, and for every $n\geq1$ the reduction $M\otimes^L_{\mathcal O_E}A_{E,n}$ lies in $D^b_c(Y,A_{E,n})$ [def-weil-finite-torsion-constructibility], with cohomological supports in one interval independent of $n$.

proof.text: Write $A=\mathcal O_E$, $P_n=A_{E,n}$. The proper factor $p:\bar X\to Y$ is finite type; composing finite affine covers and their finite algebra generators makes $\bar X/K_0$ finite type [def-weil-compactifications-refinements, def-weil-proper-morphism, def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. A field is Noetherian, so $X,Y,\bar X$ are Noetherian [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian]. Their opens are quasi-compact [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-open-subscheme-noetherian]; thus $j$ is quasi-compact. Choose its reduced closed complement [lem-weil-pbc-closed-subset-closed-subscheme].

Set $L=JK=j_!K$ over completed coefficients, identified on the open by [lem-weil-pbc-profinite-coefficient-inverse-image]. Identify the open site with its slice [lem-weil-proetale-weakly-etale-localization]. On a K-flat resolution [lem-pc-kflat-resolution], [lem-sf-ringed-open-total-tensor-kflat] makes $JQ$ a K-flat resolution of $L$. The resulting $\alpha_n:L_n\cong j_!K_n$ are precisely [lem-sf-integral-open-reduction-comparison]; they preserve quotient transitions and reduction units, computed by $q\otimes a\mapsto q\otimes\rho_n(a)$ and $q\mapsto q\otimes1$ [lem-weil-integral-reduction-tower-well-defined].

source.place: Stacks Tag 0E8I, K-flat representatives and quotient units

proof.text: Apply [lem-sf-ringed-open-roos-preservation] to the completeness triangle of $K$ [def-weil-derived-complete]; its terms are $J\operatorname{Res}_nK_n$. Both $j_!$ (completed and finite level) sheafify the extension-by-zero presheaf [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-ringed-open-closed], and module sheafification is abelian sheafification with its unique scalar action [lem-pc-sites-module-sheafification-interface]; so $J\operatorname{Res}_n=\operatorname{Res}_nj_!$. Step 2 then identifies the terms, projections and first map with the reduction tower and units of $L$; the middle map is $1-s$ for its transitions. Hence $L$ is derived complete.

source.place: Lemma 6.1.13 and the completion Roos triangle

proof.text: The hypothesis gives constructible $K_n$ in one interval $[a,b]$ [def-weil-derived-complete-integral-detailed]. By [lem-sf-open-finite-constructibility-interval], $L_n\cong j_!K_n$ are constructible in that interval. With step 3 this is $L\in D^b_c(\bar X,A)$.

Apply [lem-sf-integral-direct-image-constructible] to $p,L$: $T=Rp_*L\in D^b_c(Y,A)$, with reduction interval $[a,b+N]$ independent of $n$. Step 1 verifies its field-base finite-type hypotheses. By [def-weil-derived-direct-image], $T$ is a derived limit of $N_n=\operatorname{Res}_nRp_{*,n}L_n$ with quotient transitions.
By [lem-sf-compact-support-proper-image-tower], the $\alpha_n$ induce $N_\bullet\cong M_\bullet$ with exactly the transitions specified in the statement.

For every derived limit $M$ in the statement, [lem-weil-derived-limit-morphism] extends this system isomorphism to the Roos triangles of $T,M$; [lem-weil-derived-limit-levelwise-iso] makes $T\to M$ invertible. Isomorphism closure [lem-weil-integral-constructible-triangulated] gives $M\in D^b_c(Y,A)$, which means all three claimed properties [def-weil-derived-complete-integral-detailed].
